# Decomposition proposal: Bookshop sales insights

**Status: waiting for the owner's OK.** Nothing has been created in `plans/functional/`. The vision
has not been moved or marked `decomposed`. This agent cannot run JavaScript, so the stubs must be
created by the session through `src/lib/vision-decomposer.js`. The exact calls are in "What the
session runs next". The Product Owner handoff and `completeVision` happen only after the owner
approves.

## What I read first

- **Vision:** `plans/vision/bookshop-sales-insights.md`, read in full.
- **Canvas:** none. Glob `plans/**/*` from the project root matched 1 file, the vision. There is no
  `plans/canvas/` directory, so goals were extracted from the vision alone.
- **Code:** Glob `**/*` from the project root matched 2 files: the vision and

  greenfield project.
- **Library:** `src/lib/vision-decomposer.js` is not in this project. My request to read the plugin

  not granted. The function names and parameters below come from the agent definition, not from the

## Readiness gate (my reading; the session must run `validateVisionReadiness` for the real verdict)

| Check | Kind | In the vision |
|---|---|---|
| Problem statement | blocking | Present. Owners reorder from memory, run out of bestsellers, and slow sellers stay on the shelf |
| Target audience | blocking | Present. Owners of independent bookshops with 1 to 3 shops whose till exports weekly CSV |
| Success criteria | blocking | Present. Two criteria, both timed: import within 2 minutes, reorder within 10 minutes |
| Scope / boundaries | warning | Present. Both an In list and an Out list |
| `type: vision` marker | warning | Present in the frontmatter, plus a `## Vision:` heading |

My judgement is that the vision is specific enough to decompose. Both success criteria can be
measured with a stopwatch, and the scope names three concrete capabilities.

## Why two stubs, and why the report stub depends on the import stub

- The two success criteria have the same actor (the owner) but different impacts. One is getting
  the sales in (capture). The other is deciding the reorder (decision). That makes two goals.
- The vision says the report is "built from the sales they imported". The report goal needs the
  import goal, but the import goal does not need the report goal. The dependency runs one way only,
  so the goals are coupled loosely enough for one stub per goal, with `depends_on` from the report
  stub to the import stub.
- **This dependency cannot be removed without breaking the vision.** A report built from anything
  other than imported sales is not what the vision asks for. Two story edges cross between the stubs:
  - "See the month's bestsellers" and "See the month's slow sellers" both need "Import a week's
    export and keep its sales".
  - "See one shop or all shops together" needs "Say which shop an export came from".
- I considered merging the goals and rejected it. A single stub would hold 17 stories, which is over
  the 15-story limit for a stub, and the limit would force it to be split again. A single stub would
  also send the vision back to the Vision Advisor's single-plan path.

```markdown
## Decomposition

Parent vision: `vision/bookshop-sales-insights.md`. This goal traces to success criterion 1.
`[MVP]` marks a story on the thinnest end-to-end path. It is **not a schedule**: what is built,
and when, is the owner's decision.

### Goal: Every week's till sales are in the system within two minutes of export
- **Actor:** Owner of an independent bookshop (one to three shops) whose till exports weekly sales as CSV
- **Impact:** Brings each week's sales in from the export file instead of leaving the file unread; never retypes or cleans the file
- **Success metric:** In a timed test with a real one-week export, the time from starting the import to seeing it confirmed is under 2 minutes. Every readable line in the file is stored, and every unreadable line is listed (lines stored + lines listed = lines in the file).

### Activities (Backbone)
1. Bring in the week's export
2. Check what was imported
3. Put a wrong import right

### Activity: Bring in the week's export

**Walking Skeleton:**
- [ ] [MVP] **IMP-1 · Import a week's export and keep its sales**: As an owner, I want to choose the week's CSV export from my till and have its sales kept, so that I never have to read or retype the file.
  - Acceptance: Take a fixture export with a header row and 120 sale lines dated 21–27 September 2026, with the columns sale date, ISBN, title and copies. When the owner chooses the file and confirms, 120 sale lines are stored, each with those four values. After the application is closed and reopened, the 120 lines are still there. On the fixture, the time from choosing the file to the stored result is under 2 minutes.
  - Also sets up the application and the sales storage, because the project has no code yet. There is no separate technical story or stub for this.
  - Depends on: none (this is the foundation story)
  - INVEST: I ✓ no dependencies · N ✓ no interface or technology prescribed · V ✓ the week's sales are captured · E ✓ 5 points · S ⚠ at the 5-point limit because it carries the set-up. If planning sizes it over 3 days, split it so that it reads one fixed column layout only; never split it into a story that only adds storage · T ✓

**Additional Stories:**
- [ ] **IMP-2 · Say which shop an export came from**: As an owner of two or three shops, I want to say which shop an export came from when I import it, so that each shop's sales stay separate.
  - Acceptance: The first time, the owner types a shop name. Later imports offer the names already used. File A imported for "High Street" stores every one of its lines under High Street. File B imported for "Station Road" stores every one of its lines under Station Road. An owner with one shop is never asked.
  - Depends on: IMP-1
  - INVEST: I ✓ needs only IMP-1 · N ✓ · V ✓ shops are kept apart · E ✓ 2 points · S ✓ · T ✓
- [ ] **IMP-3 · Map my till's columns once**: As an owner whose till names or orders its columns differently, I want to tell the import once which column holds the sale date, ISBN, title and copies, so that my till's export works without editing the file.
  - Acceptance: An export with the header `Item;EAN;Qty;Date` is not recognised automatically. The owner assigns the four columns, and the file imports. The next export with the same header imports without asking.
  - Depends on: IMP-1
  - INVEST: I ✓ needs only IMP-1 · N ✓ · V ✓ other tills work · E ✓ 3 points · S ✓ · T ✓
- [ ] **IMP-4 · Accept the file exactly as the till writes it**: As an owner, I want the import to read the export whether it uses commas or semicolons, quoted titles, and UTF-8 or Windows-1252 text, so that I never have to clean the file before importing.
  - Acceptance: Three fixtures are used: comma-separated UTF-8 with a byte-order mark; semicolon-separated Windows-1252; and a file with quoted titles that contain the separator, such as `"Eats, Shoots & Leaves"`. Each fixture imports all of its lines, and accented titles such as "Café de Flore" appear correctly.
  - Depends on: IMP-1
  - INVEST: I ✓ needs only IMP-1 · N ✓ · V ✓ no manual clean-up · E ✓ 2 points · S ✓ · T ✓

### Activity: Check what was imported

**Walking Skeleton:**
- [ ] [MVP] **IMP-5 · See what was just imported**: As an owner, I want a short confirmation straight after importing, showing the week covered, the number of sale lines, the copies sold and the number of different titles, so that I know the week is in without opening the file.
  - Acceptance: For the 120-line fixture, the confirmation shows the week 21–27 September 2026. Its line, copy and title counts equal counts worked out separately from the fixture. The confirmation appears with no further action from the owner.
  - Depends on: IMP-1
  - INVEST: I ✓ needs only IMP-1 · N ✓ · V ✓ the owner trusts the import · E ✓ 1 point · S ✓ · T ✓

**Additional Stories:**
- [ ] **IMP-6 · Keep the good lines when some lines can't be read**: As an owner, I want lines the import can't read to be listed with their line number and the reason, while every other line is imported, so that one bad line doesn't stop my week.
  - Acceptance: Take a fixture with 118 good lines, one line whose copies value is "two", and one line with neither ISBN nor title. The import stores 118 lines and lists the 2 rejected lines with their line numbers and the reasons "copies is not a whole number" and "no ISBN or title". A line with −1 copies (a return) is imported, not rejected.
  - Depends on: IMP-1
  - INVEST: I ✓ needs only IMP-1 · N ✓ · V ✓ partial files still count · E ✓ 2 points · S ✓ · T ✓

### Activity: Put a wrong import right

**Walking Skeleton:**
- [ ] [MVP] **IMP-7 · Remove an import made by mistake**: As an owner, I want to remove an import I made by mistake, choosing it from the list of my imports, so that wrong sales never count in a report.
  - Acceptance: The list of imports shows the shop, week and copies for each import. After the owner removes the 21–27 September import and confirms, none of its lines are stored, and the stored copies for that shop and week are 0.
  - Depends on: IMP-1
  - INVEST: I ✓ needs only IMP-1 · N ✓ · V ✓ mistakes can be undone · E ✓ 2 points · S ✓ · T ✓

**Additional Stories:**
- [ ] **IMP-8 · Be warned before importing the same week twice**: As an owner, I want a warning before an import whose week overlaps one already imported for the same shop, so that sales are never counted twice.
  - Acceptance: Importing the 21–27 September fixture a second time shows a warning that names the existing import. Choosing Cancel, the default, leaves the stored sales unchanged. Choosing "Import anyway" adds the lines; this covers a till that splits one week across two files.
  - Depends on: IMP-1
  - INVEST: I ✓ needs only IMP-1 · N ✓ · V ✓ no double counting · E ✓ 2 points · S ✓ · T ✓
- [ ] **IMP-9 · Replace an import with a corrected export**: As an owner, I want to replace an import with a corrected export in one step, so that fixing a week doesn't mean removing it and then importing again.
  - Acceptance: Replacing the 21–27 September import (120 lines) with a corrected file of 121 lines leaves exactly 121 lines for that shop and week. If the new file can't be read at all, the original import stays as it was.
  - Depends on: IMP-7, which provides the list of imports and the removal
  - INVEST: I ✓ needs only this activity's walking-skeleton story · N ✓ · V ✓ one-step correction · E ✓ 2 points · S ✓ · T ✓

### Dependencies (story level)
- IMP-1: none
- IMP-2, IMP-3, IMP-4, IMP-5, IMP-6, IMP-7, IMP-8: depend on IMP-1
- IMP-9: depends on IMP-7
- Stories in the other stub that depend on this stub: "See the month's bestsellers" and "See the month's slow sellers" (on IMP-1), and "See one shop or all shops together" (on IMP-2).

### Dependency order for this goal (technical order, not a schedule)
1. IMP-1
2. IMP-2, IMP-3, IMP-4, IMP-5, IMP-6, IMP-7, IMP-8
3. IMP-9

Longest chain in this stub: IMP-1 → IMP-7 → IMP-9 (3 stories). There are no cycles.

## Decisions Taken Under Ambiguity
- **The till's export layout is assumed.** I assume a header row and one row per sale line, with sale date, ISBN or EAN, title and copies. IMP-1 reads that one layout; IMP-3 maps other layouts. A real export from the owner's till would confirm or correct this.
- **Each book is identified by its ISBN or EAN.** When a line has neither, the exact title text is used.
- **An import covers the Monday-to-Sunday week or weeks that contain its sale dates.** A day the shop is closed is still counted as covered, so it is never reported as missing.
- **Returns are lines with negative copies.** They are stored, and they reduce the copies sold.
- **When an import overlaps an existing one, the owner is warned and Cancel is the default.** "Import anyway" exists for tills that split one week across two files.
- **When some lines can't be read, the rest of the file is still imported.** Each rejected line is listed with its line number and the reason.
- **Shops are tagged at import time.** An owner with one shop is never asked.
- **IMP-1 carries the application and storage set-up**, because there is no code yet. A separate technical stub would be a horizontal slice, which the method rules out.
- **"Independent" in INVEST is read as follows:** an additional story may depend on its activity's walking-skeleton story or on the foundation story, but never on a sibling enhancement.
```

### Block to insert into Stub 2 (one `Edit`, placed just before its `## Scope` heading)

```markdown
## Decomposition

Parent vision: `vision/bookshop-sales-insights.md`. This goal traces to success criterion 2.
`[MVP]` marks a story on the thinnest end-to-end path. It is **not a schedule**: what is built,
and when, is the owner's decision.

**This stub depends on "Import weekly till sales".** The report is built only from imported sales,
so it has nothing to show until that stub's IMP-1 ("Import a week's export and keep its sales")
exists.

### Goal: Reorders are decided from a monthly report in under ten minutes
- **Actor:** Owner of an independent bookshop (one to three shops)
- **Impact:** Reorders bestsellers from the sales data and stops reordering slow sellers, instead of reordering from memory
- **Success metric:** With a month of imported sales, the time from opening the month's report to holding a finished reorder list (printed or saved) is under 10 minutes in a timed test.

### Activities (Backbone)
1. Read the month's report
2. Make the reorder list

### Activity: Read the month's report

**Walking Skeleton:**
- [ ] [MVP] **REP-1 · See the month's bestsellers**: As an owner, I want to open the report for a month and see its bestsellers, meaning titles ranked by copies sold that month in the sales I imported, so that I know what to reorder first.
  - Acceptance: The imported fixture sales for September are Title A 31 copies, Title B 22, Title C 22 and Title D 3. The September report lists A first, then B and C (equal copies, so ordered A–Z by title), each with ISBN, title and copies. At most 20 titles are listed. Only sale lines dated in September count. From the export covering 28 September–4 October, lines dated 28–30 September count and lines dated 1–4 October do not. Returns reduce a title's copies. When no sales have been imported for the month, the report says so instead of showing an empty list.
  - Whichever of REP-1 and REP-2 is built first also creates the month report and the way to choose a month.
  - Depends on: IMP-1 in the stub "Import weekly till sales"
  - INVEST: I ✓ independent of REP-2 · N ✓ · V ✓ the owner sees what to reorder · E ✓ 3 points · S ✓ · T ✓
- [ ] [MVP] **REP-2 · See the month's slow sellers**: As an owner, I want to see the month's slow sellers, meaning titles that sold in an earlier imported month but sold at most one copy this month, so that I stop reordering books that sit on the shelf.
  - Acceptance: Title E sold 4 copies in August and none in September, so it is listed for September with "last sold 17 August 2026" (the date comes from the fixture). Title F sold 6 in August and 1 in September, so it is listed. Title G first sold in September (1 copy, no earlier sales), so it is not listed. The list is ordered oldest last-sale first. For the first month with imported sales, the report says that slow sellers need at least one earlier month of imported sales.
  - Both REP-1 and REP-2 are marked `[MVP]` because success criterion 2 names bestsellers and slow sellers together.
  - Depends on: IMP-1 in the stub "Import weekly till sales"
  - INVEST: I ✓ independent of REP-1 · N ✓ · V ✓ the owner stops reordering slow sellers · E ✓ 3 points · S ✓ · T ✓

**Additional Stories:**
- [ ] **REP-3 · Be told when a week of the month has no imported sales**: As an owner, I want the month's report to say which weeks of the month no import covers, so that I don't reorder from an incomplete month.
  - Acceptance: With imports for every September week except 14–20 September, the September report shows "No sales imported for the week of 14–20 September" above the lists. When every week is covered, no notice appears.
  - Depends on: REP-1
  - INVEST: I ✓ needs only the walking skeleton · N ✓ · V ✓ prevents decisions on partial data · E ✓ 2 points · S ✓ · T ✓
- [ ] **REP-4 · See one shop or all shops together**: As an owner of two or three shops, I want to choose one shop or all shops for the month's report, so that I can reorder per shop or for the whole business.
  - Acceptance: September sales are imported for High Street (Title A: 20) and Station Road (Title A: 11). The High Street report shows Title A with 20, Station Road shows 11, and All shops shows 31. An owner with one shop is not offered the choice. Once the slow-seller list exists, it follows the same choice.
  - Depends on: REP-1, and IMP-2 in the stub "Import weekly till sales"
  - INVEST: I ✓ two dependencies, the maximum allowed · N ✓ · V ✓ reordering per shop · E ✓ 2 points · S ✓ · T ✓
- [ ] **REP-5 · Set the list length and the slow-seller threshold**: As an owner, I want to set how many bestsellers are listed and the most copies a slow seller may have sold, so that the lists fit the size of my shop.

  - INVEST: I ✓ needs only the two walking-skeleton stories · N ✓ · V ✓ fits shops of different sizes · E ✓ 2 points · S ✓ · T ✓

### Activity: Make the reorder list

**Walking Skeleton:**
- [ ] [MVP] **REP-6 · Build and print a reorder list from the report**: As an owner, I want to tick titles on the bestseller list to put them on a reorder list with a quantity, prefilled with the copies sold that month, and print that list, so that I can place my orders from paper.

2. REP-3, REP-4, REP-5, REP-6

Longest chain inside this stub: REP-1 → REP-6 → REP-7 (3 stories). Counting the other stub,
the longest chain is IMP-1 → REP-1 → REP-6 → REP-7, and the same for REP-8 (4 stories). See the
decision on dependency depth below. There are no cycles.

## Decisions Taken Under Ambiguity
- **A sale counts in the month of its own sale date.** An export week that crosses a month boundary is split line by line.
- **Bestsellers are titles ranked by copies sold in the month.** By default 20 are listed; ties are ordered A–Z by title.
- **Slow sellers are titles with imported sales in an earlier month that sold 1 copy or fewer this month.** They are ordered oldest last-sale first. Limitation: sales data only contains books that sold, so a book that has never sold since the owner started importing can never appear. Fixing that needs stock or catalogue data, which is not in the vision's In list.
- **The reorder quantity is prefilled with the copies sold that month.** The owner can change it.
- **The reorder list leaves the system by print (REP-6) or as a CSV file (REP-7).** Ordering from suppliers is excluded by the vision.
- **The report shows copies only, never money.** Neither success criterion needs money values, and the vision excludes more than one currency.
- **REP-1 and REP-2 can be built in either order.** Whichever comes first creates the month report and the way to choose a month.
- **Dependency depth across the stubs:** the chain IMP-1 → REP-1 → REP-6 → REP-7 or REP-8 is 4 stories, one more than the method's limit of 3. This follows the vision's own journey: import, then report, then reorder list, then extras on the list. The alternative is to fold REP-7 and REP-8 into REP-6, which brings the depth back to 3 but makes REP-6 about 5 points. I kept them separate; the owner decides.
- **"Independent" in INVEST is read as follows:** an additional story may depend on its activity's walking-skeleton story, but never on a sibling enhancement.
```

## Decisions that apply to the whole decomposition

1. **No canvas.** None exists, so goals were extracted from the vision alone.
2. **Readiness gate.** I checked the vision against the gate by reading it. The verdict that counts
   is the one from `validateVisionReadiness`, run by the session.
3. **No phases and no schedule.** `[MVP]` marks only the thinnest end-to-end path, which is a fact
   about the dependency graph. I did not group stories into flesh-out or polish phases. Build order
   is the owner's decision, chosen from the dependency graph.
